assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides turned DNA polymerase chemistry into a massively parallel readout and reshaped genomics, cancer biology and genome-maintenance research, including work like mine on mutation and replication fidelity. The chemistry (engineered nucleotides, polymerase incorporation, fluorophore cleavage) is a clearly defined reaction scheme that biologists adopted broadly.
assessment.attribution: The Cambridge pair (Balasubramanian and Klenerman) conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach. Rothberg (pyrosequencing/454) and Mayer address parallel but distinct platforms, so a two-person prize on the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Exceptionally mature: independently reproduced on many instruments, with two decades of routine use and clinical deployment; recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views next-generation sequencing as chemistry or as an instrument/biology technology; the credit boundary against the 454 and nanopore platforms is a design choice rather than a settled fact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base into another (cytosine or adenine deamination on a Cas-bound single strand) without double-strand breaks, a mechanism-defined chemical tool with direct therapeutic use. The directed-evolution engineering of an adenine deaminase acting on DNA is a distinctive chemical-biology achievement.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu is the clear intellectual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine editors respectively, and the Japanese work (Nishida, Kondo) on deaminase-Cas9 fusions is a parallel contribution. A single-laureate prize is defensible; if broadened, the allocation relative to the CRISPR prize already given is a sensitivity.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many laboratories and now in clinical trials with first patient data; interpretation is stable, though long-term safety and off-target deamination are still being measured. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap in public perception with the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize.
Long-term clinical outcomes and off-target (including RNA and bystander) editing remain incompletely characterised, and I am not independently verifying clinical status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues recast pharmacology as event-driven, catalytic hijacking of the ubiquitin-proteasome system, making formerly undruggable targets accessible. The key chemical idea (induced proximity via a small molecule) is general and mechanistically well defined, including the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and launched the PROTAC concept (Sakamoto, Kim also credited), while Ciulli contributed the VHL ligand structural basis and rational design. Handa and Ito elucidated cereblon as the thalidomide target, a separate molecular-glue discovery, so the candidate is a compound one and the prize configuration is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism broadly confirmed by multiple groups with structures and numerous clinical-stage degraders; clinical approval is still pending, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTACs versus the cereblon/glue mechanism may merit different recognition.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes recognition premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's tethering of covalent inhibitors to the mutant cysteine of KRAS G12C, found in the switch-II pocket, overturned the view of RAS as undruggable and led directly to approved drugs; his earlier analogue-sensitive kinase chemical genetics is also a general tool. It is a clear chemistry-to-biology and medicine story.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean: a single credited name with decisive, well-documented primary contributions. Downstream drug companies (Amgen, Mirati) built on his discovery, but the foundational mechanism is his.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently, with approved covalent KRAS G12C inhibitors, so maturity and timeliness are strong.
uncertainties: Industrial contributions to the approved drugs could complicate how the committee frames the discovery.
I am relying on general knowledge about approval status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A methylation of RNA, with writers, erasers and readers, opened an epitranscriptomic layer of regulation and defined the chemistry of a modification on RNA. This is a molecular process turned into a defined enzymatic system with broad biological and disease relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chuan He's group defined FTO as an m6A demethylase and conceptualised reversible RNA modification; Jaffrey and Rechavi mapped m6A transcriptome-wide in 2012, with others (Jia, Meyer, Dominissini, Yang) credited. Allocation among mapping and enzymology contributions is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations of writers and readers, but quantitative stoichiometry, antibody-based mapping artefacts and the physiological role of some erasers have been debated, so as a careful measurement-oriented member I rate it a bit short of fully mature.
uncertainties: Dispute over transcriptome-wide mapping accuracy and over ALKBH5/FTO substrate specificity.
Credit among enzyme discovery and mapping groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the foundation of chemical DNA synthesis, underpinning primers, oligonucleotide therapeutics, synthetic biology and sequencing, and every nucleotide-metabolism and replication laboratory depends on it. The reaction is well defined and has proven durable for four decades.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method; Beaucage and Hood's automation role complicate credit. Hood is credited here, but the decisive chemistry is Caruthers's, so a single-name prize fits best, with the allocation relative to Beaucage (not on the supplied list) unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and overdue; independently validated by universal use, though it is not a current scientific frontier.
uncertainties: Absent credited co-originators (such as Beaucage) in the supplied names complicate fairness.
The committee may regard it as too old or too much a method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing led to electrical reading of single DNA or RNA molecules and long-read sequencing, with potential for direct detection of modified bases, meaning direct measurement of nucleic-acid chemistry. The engineered protein pores and motor-enzyme control are original and consequential.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated single-strand translocation; Bayley engineered pores; Akeson showed controlled enzymatic ratcheting. Credit is distributed across stages and Branton may no longer be eligible, so a defensible three-person set is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Technology is established and widely adopted, with independent validation; accuracy has improved over time, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether Branton's eligibility and the Oxford Nanopore commercial development affect the configuration.
Overlap with next-generation sequencing as a sibling candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled delivery of siRNA and mRNA medicines, a prerequisite for the vaccines recognised in 2023 and for oligonucleotide drugs such as patisiran. The pH-dependent ionisation behaviour of the lipids is a concrete chemical design principle.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope and colleagues developed the lipid-nanoparticle formulation and ionizable lipid concepts; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid design. Allocation between formulation and lipid-chemistry contributors is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Validated at scale clinically, so the confirmation is strong, and recognition is timely after the 2023 mRNA prize.
uncertainties: Possible perception that the 2023 prize already covers it, and unclear boundaries between pharmaceutical engineering and chemistry.
Credit distribution among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer.
